title: Shortness of Breath

correct_orders.rationale: Helps symptoms, not outcomes. For moderate-severe CHF (NYHA III-IV) as adjunct.

rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: Dyspnea + cardiac history — S3 gallop, JVD.
rationale.Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine: Pitting edema — hallmark of R-sided HF.
rationale.TSH: Thyroid pathology associated with arrhythmias precipitating HF.
rationale.Cardiac troponin: Superimposed ischemia/infarction is common cause of HF exacerbation.
rationale.Chest X-ray: Pulmonary edema + cardiomegaly. Rule out other causes of dyspnea.
rationale.Echocardiography: Confirms CHF — reduced ejection fraction (systolic dysfunction).
rationale.Stress test / Stress echo: NO stress tests until patient recovers from acute HF exacerbation.
rationale.Furosemide (Lasix) / Bumetanide / Torsem: Volume overloaded — loop diuretic for rapid symptom improvement.
rationale.Digoxin: Helps symptoms, not outcomes. For moderate-severe CHF (NYHA III-IV) as adjunct.
rationale.Nitroglycerin: Dilates coronary arteries — reduces afterload and improves coronary flow.
rationale.Beta-blocker (Carvedilol / Metoprolol /: Start after diuresis, prior to discharge. Carvedilol preferred (COMET trial: 17% survival benefit over metoprolol). All 3 accepted.
rationale.Stress test during acute exacerbation: Stress tests contraindicated until acute CHF exacerbation resolves. Risk of decompensation.
rationale.Beta-blocker BEFORE diuresis: Beta-blocker should be started after patient is euvolemic (post-diuresis), before discharge. Starting during acute volume overload can worsen hemodynamics.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is an older man with history of prior myocardial infarction and hypertension on lisinopril who presents with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, PND, and bilateral lower extremity pitting edema. Exam reveals JVD, S3 gallop, pulmonary crackles, and expiratory wheezing. CXR shows pulmonary edema and cardiomegaly. Echo confirms reduced ejection fraction — systolic dysfunction. BNP is elevated. The most common cause of systolic HF is ischemic heart disease. NYHA Class III-IV (symptoms with minimal activity). Treatment: IV loop diuretic (furosemide) for volume overload, continue ACEI, add nitroglycerin for afterload reduction. Once acute exacerbation resolves and patient is euvolemic, start beta-blocker (carvedilol preferred per COMET trial — 17% survival benefit over metoprolol, though bisoprolol and metoprolol succinate also accepted). Digoxin for symptom control if needed. No stress tests until recovered. Admit to inpatient unit. Discharge: low-sodium diet, smoking cessation, alcohol avoidance, pneumococcal and zoster vaccines, Tdap.
